subject: Proposed GPU pool sizing & discount structure for Skyline Robotics — workload breakdown
content:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@skyline-robotics.com>, procurement@skyline-robotics.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial workload details & ask: Dedicated GPU pool sizing for inference

Hi Daniel / Skyline team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — good to see the real-time control loop use case in action. As promised, I pulled together a compact workload profile to start the sizing conversation for a Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool. Attached: skyline_workload_profile.xlsx and sample_prompts.json.

Quick notes up front:
- Request volume (p50/p95): 9k / 38k requests per hour during peak windows.
- Typical context length: 1.2k tokens average; some validation jobs spike to ~8k.
- Latency target: 95th %ile <= 220ms for the control-plane model (chat/generation), lower SLO for batch scoring jobs.
- Concurrency pattern: tens of long-lived LLM sessions (~300 persistent sessions), plus bursts from webhooks.

Can you confirm: expected average tokens per request and % of requests that need full 8k context? That will determine whether we recommend an nGPU pool optimized for long-context models versus more smaller instances for throughput.

Next steps from our side: we will produce two options — (A) baseline pool sized for your p95 traffic with a conservative 10% headroom and (B) cost-optimized pool assuming 20% traffic smoothing via caching and batching. I expect to share a formal pricing + commit recommendation by Monday.

Best,

Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attach: skyline_workload_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
attach: sample_prompts.json (json, 14KB)

---

From: Daniel Park <daniel@skyline-robotics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skyline-robotics.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial workload details & ask: Dedicated GPU pool sizing for inference

Thanks, Aisha — great summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Tokens per request: the control loop messages average ~900 tokens, but the telemetry-enriched prompts (used for diagnostics) average closer to 3.5k. We estimate ~12% of requests are the heavy telemetry ones.
2) The 8k spikes are for nightly validation runs (approx 40 jobs per night) and can be scheduled outside of peak windows. They can tolerate higher latency (up to 2s).
3) Important: procurement needs a clear committed monthly spend band and a discount tier based on committed GPU-hours. We are evaluating 12- and 24-month commits.

Daniel
Director of Engineering, Skyline Robotics

---

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@skyline-robotics.com>, procurement@skyline-robotics.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial workload details & ask: Dedicated GPU pool sizing for inference

Thanks Daniel — that helps a lot. Based on your clarifications, we ran two candidate sizing models and cost scenarios. Summary (high level):

Option A — Performance-first (recommended for low tail latency)
- Pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed 80GB nodes), configured for low-latency continuous batching.
- Expected steady throughput: ~55k requests/hour (p95) at 900–3.5k token mix with 10% headroom.
- Nightly validation: offloaded to burst capacity (on-demand) to avoid oversizing the dedicated pool.
- Commit: 12-month reserved commit, monthly minimum: 6200 GPU-hours.
- Pricing: list rate 18% below hosted-per-token baseline for committed usage; with a 12-month commit we can offer a further 12% contract discount (stacked), bringing effective discount to ~28% vs hosted.

Option B — Cost-optimized (assumes batching/caching gains)
- Pool: 5x A100-equivalent GPUs, with opportunistic burst to on-demand for validation jobs.
- Expected steady throughput: ~38k req/hour (p95) assuming 20% latency-tolerant traffic and smart prefix caching.
- Commit: 12- or 24-month options; 24-month commit reduces unit price further.
- Pricing: list rate ~30% below hosted baseline for the committed hours; 24-month commit + volume >9000 GPU-hours/month yields an incremental 8% discount.

Operational notes:
- We recommend pinning a control-plane model for latency-sensitive routes and keeping a smaller, quantized variant for best-effort scoring to reduce tail risk.
- Autoscaling policy: warm standby GPUs for predictable burst handling (we price warm standby at ~40% of active GPU-hours for committed pools).
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime on dedicated pools under a 12-month contract; additional credits available for 24-month enterprise contracts.

Attached is a short pdf (proposal_gpu_pool.pdf) with the math and expected per-token/unit economics. I also included a sample commit schedule for ramp months.

Action items for procurement: please confirm which commit term you're considering (12 vs 24 months) and whether the warm-standby policy is acceptable — that will lock the monthly minimum.

Thanks — looping in Ben (discount approvals) and Marcus (engineering fit) to ensure pricing and pool design are aligned.

Cheers,

Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attach: proposal_gpu_pool.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: aisha@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing structure for Skyline Robotics — internal note

Aisha — reviewed the numbers. Two quick internal points:

1) Discounting: given the deal size and strategic fit (robotics edge customer, likely expansion into EU), I can approve up to an extra 3% off the quoted effective discount for a 24-month commit, provided we lock a minimum 9k GPU-hours/month. Anything beyond that requires rev-level signoff.
2) Upsell path: ask for a pilot to validate caching gains; if they commit to a 6-month pilot that proves the 20% traffic smoothing, we can convert Option B to a 24-month plan with backdated pricing adjustments.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---

From: procurement@skyline-robotics.com
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed GPU pool sizing & discount structure for Skyline Robotics — workload breakdown

Hi Aisha / Ben / Marcus,

Thank you — procurement has reviewed and discussed internally. Skyline is prepared to proceed with Option B on a 24-month commit, contingent on the following:

- Monthly minimum to be set at 9,000 GPU-hours with the incremental 8% discount you outlined (we expect the math to match the proposal pdf).
- Warm-standby pricing must be capped at 40% of active GPU-hours as noted.
- A 3-month pilot period where Redwood will provide engineering support to implement prefix caching and batching recommendations; during the pilot we will pay the committed monthly minimum, and if caching gains are >=15% we will accelerate the transition to full routing rules.

Please confirm acceptance in writing and send the draft MSA/Order Form with the specific commit line items for signature.

Regards,

Procurement Team
Skyline Robotics
attach: PO-intent-skyline.pdf (pdf, 12KB)
